title: Does Vinyl Plank Flooring Scratch? What Actually Damages LVP
meta: Vinyl plank does scratch, but rarely from dogs or kids. Wills Flooring explains what really damages LVP in busy Sammamish homes and how wear layer changes it.
keywords: does vinyl plank flooring scratch, LVP scratch resistance, vinyl plank wear layer dogs, what damages luxury vinyl plank, vinyl plank flooring Sammamish WA

blocks.lead: Yes, vinyl plank scratches, but a 20 mil wear layer shrugs off dog nails, kids and daily grit. What actually damages LVP is dragged furniture, trapped sand, rubber mats and rolling chairs.
blocks.detail: On the Sammamish plateau, where a typical house has two kids, a big dog and an open-plan main floor, we see far more gouges from a moved fridge than from any pet. Pick the right wear layer and protect a few specific spots and LVP stays clean for years.

blocks.html: The fear behind this question is usually a photo online of a vinyl floor with a white scratch across three planks. That happens. It almost never happens from the things people worry about. Below is what we have watched damage LVP in Klahanie, Trossachs and Pine Lake homes over the years, ranked honestly, plus what the wear layer number on the box really buys you and what to do when a plank does get gouged.

blocks.text: What really scratches vinyl plank, ranked

items.title: Furniture dragged, not lifted
items.text: A sectional pushed across the room on plastic feet, or a fridge walked out for the water line, leaves the deep white gouges that show in every scary photo. The wear layer is cut through and the core is exposed. No wear layer thickness prevents this. Felt pads and sliders do.

items.title: Grit tracked in from outside
items.text: Sammamish driveways shed sand and gravel all winter, and the plateau's trail network sends it home on boots and paws. Ground underfoot at the entry and the kitchen slider, grit works like fine sandpaper. Over a couple of years it dulls the finish in a path you can see in low light.

items.title: Dog nails
items.text: An 80 lb dog skidding to the front door leaves faint scuffs in the top coat on a 12 mil floor and almost nothing on a 20 mil floor. The scuffs are in the clear coat, not through it, and most disappear with a damp mop. Nails that click on the floor are due for a trim.

items.title: Rolling chairs and rubber
items.text: Hard-caster office chairs wear a dull halo into the plank under a desk within a year. Rubber-backed rugs and rubber chair mats do something worse: they react with the vinyl and leave a permanent yellow stain that no cleaner removes. Use felt-backed rugs and polycarbonate chair mats.

blocks.text: What the wear layer number actually means

head: Wear layer
Where it belongs
How it handles a Sammamish household
rows: Dog nails leave visible scuffs within months. Fine for a guest room, wrong for a main floor.
Bedrooms, home offices without rolling chairs
Handles kids and a small dog. A large dog and a mudroom entry will show a traffic path in three to five years.
Main floors, kitchens, entries, any home with a big dog
The plateau standard. Grit and nails stay in the clear coat instead of the print layer. This is what we recommend for Klahanie and Trossachs family homes.
Commercial, ADUs used as rentals, very heavy dogs
Overkill for most houses, but the price gap to 20 mil has narrowed. Worth it if you run a daycare or board dogs.
blocks.note: Wear layer is the clear top coat measured in thousandths of an inch. Total plank thickness is a different number and matters less for scratches.

items.text: 20 mil rigid core through the main floor, felt-backed runners at both doors, dog nails trimmed monthly. Four years in, we found two scuffs under the kitchen table and nothing else.
12 mil plank chosen to save money. A hard-caster chair and a rubber mat left a dull ring and a yellow rectangle in eighteen months. We swapped nine planks and they switched to a polycarbonate mat.

items.text: New 20 mil floor, then the homeowners slid the fridge back themselves on its bare feet. Two deep gouges the first day. Click-lock let us replace three planks; a glue-down floor would have been harder.

blocks.text: When LVP is not tough enough, and what beats it

a.title: Choose vinyl plank when
items: The threats are pets, kids, water and grit
You want a floor that hides small marks in the texture
Rooms are open-plan and see mud and rain from the slider
You are fine replacing a plank instead of refinishing a floor

b.title: Reconsider when
items: You expect to drag heavy furniture or gym equipment often
The room is a workshop, garage conversion or has metal-wheeled carts
You want a floor that can be sanded back to new after 15 years, which is hardwood
The room gets intense afternoon sun with no blinds, which fades any print layer

blocks.title: About repairability:
blocks.text: A scratched hardwood floor gets sanded. A scratched vinyl plank gets replaced, which is easy on a floating click-lock floor and fiddly on glue-down. Buy one extra carton and store it flat. Dye lots change, and a plank from the original run is the only one that will match in five years.
How to keep vinyl plank scratch-free in a busy house

items.html: Felt pads on everything that touches the floor. Chairs, table legs, the couch, the fridge if it rolls out. This single habit prevents the deepest damage we see in Sammamish homes.
Walk-off mats at the slider and the garage door. Two feet of mat removes most grit before it becomes sandpaper. Choose felt or woven backing, never rubber.
Trim nails and choose a textured plank. A wire-brushed or embossed-in-register texture hides the faint scuffs that a smooth gloss plank shows in the light off the lake.
Spend on the wear layer, not the plank thickness. A 5 mm plank with a 20 mil wear layer beats an 8 mm plank with 12 mil for scratches. Our plank thickness post covers the difference.

Ask what the quote assumes. Wills Flooring's vinyl plank installation is $2.50 per sq ft labor with a 500 sq ft minimum, and we bring 12 mil and 20 mil samples to your house so you can scratch-test them yourself.

faq.q: Does luxury vinyl plank scratch easily?
faq.a: Not easily, but it is not scratch-proof. A 20 mil wear layer resists dog nails, toys and normal grit for years. Deep scratches come from dragging furniture or appliances across the floor, which cuts through the wear layer no matter how thick it is. Felt pads and sliders prevent most of it.

faq.q: Is vinyl plank flooring good for big dogs?
faq.a: Yes, with a 20 mil or thicker wear layer and a textured surface. Large dogs leave scuffs in the clear coat that mostly mop off, and the waterproof core handles accidents and water bowls. Keep nails trimmed and use a felt-backed runner where the dog charges the front door.

faq.q: Can scratches in vinyl plank be repaired?
faq.a: Light scuffs usually clean off or blend with a vinyl floor polish. A gouge through the wear layer cannot be sanded out, so the plank is replaced. On a floating click-lock floor that is a quick job. Keep one carton from the original dye lot for exactly this reason.

faq.q: What wear layer do I need on vinyl plank for a family home?
faq.a: For main floors, kitchens and entries in a home with kids or pets, 20 mil. For bedrooms and low-traffic rooms, 12 mil is enough. Anything under 12 mil belongs in a closet or a rental, and 28 mil and up is commercial grade that most Sammamish homes do not need.

faq.q: Do rolling office chairs damage vinyl plank?
faq.a: Hard plastic casters wear a dull ring into the plank within a year and can leave fine scratches. Swap the casters for soft polyurethane wheels or use a polycarbonate chair mat. Avoid rubber chair mats, which chemically stain vinyl a permanent yellow.

faq.q: Why did my vinyl plank turn yellow under a rug?
faq.a: Rubber and latex backing on rugs and mats react with vinyl plasticizers and leave a yellow stain that is in the plank, not on it. No cleaner fixes it; the planks have to be replaced. Use rugs with felt, jute or woven polypropylene backing over LVP.
